bottleneck: Dreaming consumes hours nightly across all mammals, yet its function — memory consolidation, emotional regulation, threat simulation, or mere epiphenomenon — is unproven after a century of debate. REM sleep can be pharmacologically suppressed for long periods with surprisingly mild effects, undermining every strong theory, while targeted memory reactivation during sleep shows dreams interact with memory without revealing why the vivid narrative form exists. A universal, elaborate feature of conscious life has no agreed purpose: theories proliferate precisely because none can be falsified, and the sleeping brain's generative capacity remains unharnessed for therapy or learning.
current_state: Targeted memory reactivation during sleep shows dreams interact with memory, but no theory of dreaming commands consensus, and dream engineering for therapy is nascent.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Dream function has no consensus theory
why_it_blocks: If dreams serve memory or mental health, understanding them unlocks new therapies — from PTSD nightmare treatment to memory enhancement. If they are noise, that itself reshapes theories of consciousness. The unknown is load-bearing either way.
